method: Complete candidate survey followed by individual editorial choices and written reasons, applied to the existing complete guide to keep it within 300 quotations. All verified authorized selections included. Priority given to foundational teachings, substantive explanations, necessary qualifications, distinctive applications, narrative examples and thematic breadth across recognition, freedom and the meaning of servitude; repentance, mercy and making amends; trust, contentment and surrender; service in everyday life; ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s station and practice of service; patient service amid persecution and loss; prayers gathering the journey together; and the closing readings on contentment and attentive action. Neither citation count nor source order used as a ranking rule. Imported wording checked separately; version differences remain explicit. The existing reading arc is retained.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer that contemplating God’s greatness, He finds Himself the most rebellious of all.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh calling the reader to repent, then entrust his affairs to God and rely upon Him; the bridge from repentance to trust.

selected.reason: The Báb’s prayer that sinning or obeying He is still God’s servant; a distinctive, paradoxical statement of servitude.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer, “Draw me unto Thee, even if by chains and fetters,” to dwell with those who have no will save God’s.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh directing wrongdoers to seek God’s forgiveness seventy times and return with soul, spirit and body; a distinctive practice of return.

selected.text: How sweet is the flow of the spirit of servitude in my spirit, my essence, my being and all my limbs and parts before Thy exalted threshold! selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s prayer on the sweetness of the spirit of servitude flowing through his whole being.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer of shame at His deeds that finds rest in knowing that all comes from God.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s first counsel that the friends become his partners in servitude to the Divine Threshold.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer that though heedlessness led to the bitter waters of idle fancies, God did not forget and His loving-kindness remained ablaze; mercy answering neglect.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words of repentance, “we obeyed our leaders and our great ones” and misled the weak, asking pardon; a confession that names the harm done to others.

selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that in prayer God cleanses the heart, and asking at whose door we could knock if He closed His; hope as the ground of return.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh assuring that whoever trusts God in all things will be sufficed, for He never forsakes His loved ones; a foundational promise of trust.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing his servitude as one whose core, essence, beginning and end is servitude; opens his account of his own station.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá contrasting the crown of servitude, whose jewels come from the mine of reality, with crowns whose gems come from the mine of dust.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying he desires to adorn the gallows in the path of servitude rather than seek release from prison.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh proclaiming today the day of servitude and calling complete servitude the station that attains all good; a central affirmation of the subject.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer of shame over every movement, rest and thought, repeating “I seek Thy forgiveness”; a comprehensive act of contrition.

selected.text: True servitude is a mighty station. selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh calling true servitude a mighty station and warning that everything has a fixed station, measure and limit; carries the guide’s qualification about the bounds of servitude.

selected.text: Thou knowest, O my God, my lowliness and poverty, my destitution and need, my detachment and supplication, my humility and entreaty at the threshold of Thy oneness, and my pure servitude and absolute bondage at Thy holy doorstep. selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s prayer acknowledging his lowliness and calling pure servitude the light of his reality; its source also cites Jesus’ words leaving punishment or forgiveness of others to God.

selected.text: I testify that I was heedless - Thou didst guide me to Thy path; I was ignorant - Thou didst teach me the ways of Thy good-pleasure; I was asleep - Thou didst awaken me to Thy remembrance and praise. selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer that God guided the heedless, taught the ignorant and awakened the sleeper, with confession of powerlessness.

selected.text: O fellow worker and fellow thinker with this servant of the Threshold! selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá telling a fellow worker that servitude to the loved ones of God is freedom in both worlds and tranquility of heart.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer abasing Himself before those who seek might through God’s sovereignty, among those who repent and worship.

selected.reason: The Báb’s prayer to find sufficiency and contentment in God apart from all creation.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá inviting a woman to be a handmaiden of Bahá as he is His servant, asking what station could be greater.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá explaining that human reality, by coming into existence, made a promise to arise in servitude, and that the truthful in promise fulfills it; a distinctive account of servitude as a covenant of being.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh teaching that confession of powerlessness is the essence of worship and acknowledgment of weakness the heart’s strength; a distinctive explanation of the servant’s station.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s sequence pointing those who seek honor, strength, protection and greatness to God and to service at the Sacred Threshold.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s prayer in the Tablet of the Thousand Verses for confirmation in servitude and humility among God’s servants.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá telling the friends that if they seek his joy they should mention his servitude, which he would not exchange for sovereignty; his response to praise.

selected.text: My highest desire in this world is to be confirmed in the service of the Threshold of the Blessed Perfection. No other title or station is pleasing to me. Baha'u'llah Himself has crowned my head with the Diadem of Servitude. selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that Bahá’u’lláh crowned him with the diadem of servitude, which he would not exchange for lordship.

selected.text: The meaning of this verse is that should they call me by any name and raise their voice, that call would not harmonize with my ear nor would it be heard, save when someone addresses me as His servant - then instantly the ear becomes attentive and the mind alert
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá explaining that no name pleases his ear save being addressed as God’s servant.

selected.text: This assembly must walk in the footsteps of 'Abdu'l-Baha - must become pure nothingness, absolute effacement and sheer non-existence, that is to say, embodied servitude and personified thralldom. selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calling an assembly to walk in his footsteps as embodied servitude and personified thralldom.

selected.text: I do confess unto Thee through the supreme declarations and ultimate --- that I have not truly glorified Thee and can never glorify Thee, I have not truly praised Thee and can never exalt Thee. selected.reason: The Báb’s confession that He has not truly glorified God and can never do so; its source text retains a gap.

selected.text: My Lord! I am Thy servant who hath confessed his transgressions before the waves of Thy forgiveness and his sins before the dawning-places of the Day-Star of Thy pardon. How many nights did I sleep upon my couch, heedless of Thy manifestation and of hearkening to Thy most sweet call as it was raised between earth and heaven! And how many days was I occupied with my affairs, hesitating in Thy Cause!
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer confessing nights of heedless sleep and days of hesitation in God’s Cause before the waves of His forgiveness.

selected.text: Thou bearest witness, O my Lord, to my servitude and lowliness, to my privation and abasement, my powerlessness and destitution before the portals of Thy divine unity, and Thou beholdest my selflessness, mine evanescence and non-existence, my humility and prostration, my meekness and submissiveness, mine ardent invocation, my tearful supplication and entreaty before the Threshold of Thy mercifulness.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s prayer bearing witness to his servitude, lowliness and evanescence before God.

selected.text: Make me ready, in all circumstances, O my Lord, to serve Thee and to set myself towards the adored sanctuary of Thy Revelation and of Thy Beauty. selected.text: These are they of whom He saith: "They speak not until He hath spoken." Their hearing awaiteth the word "Listen," their eyes await the blessed word "Behold," and their tongues stand ready for the manifestation of the word "Speak," for such souls are extinct in themselves, in what they possess, in their will and desire, and are focused upon, speak of, utter and stand firm in that which God hath willed.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing souls who speak not until God has spoken and await His word to listen, behold and speak; a vivid picture of surrendered will.

selected.text: You know this servant, who from the beginning of the Cause has had no thought by day or night save to serve, according to his weakness and capacity, the Cause of God. I have not rested for a moment, nor found repose for a single night. No evening has brought me peace, no dawn has granted tranquility to my heart. At all times I have been in turmoil and strain, in all seasons in difficulty and tribulation.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing a life of service without rest amid turmoil and tribulation; a narrative of patient service.

selected.text: The glory of existence is for one to make his own will fade away in God's will - that is, to have no will, thought or imagination of his own, but to move by God's will and act accordingly. Deem not this matter imaginary. Whosoever today hath drunk of the sealed wine and acted according to that which hath proceeded from the Source of Command, hath attained unto God's will, and he is of the people of truth.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh on the glory of existence as letting one’s own will fade in God’s will, warning that this is no imaginary matter; opens the guide’s distinction between true surrender and personal imaginings.

selected.text: Indeed, if the drops of the sea could be counted and the sands of the deserts limited, these stations too would be bounded. Who can render thanks by hand or tongue? In all conditions I beseech for thee His aid and confirmation, and likewise for myself, though this too is wrong - man hath no self or self-will. He must be attentive to the Command and arise in service like a corpse in the hands of the washer.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh teaching that man has no self-will and must arise in service like a corpse in the hands of the washer; a memorable image of surrender.

selected.text: This means that they should sacrifice and immolate all that pertaineth to them for the Beauty of God so that in this way they may reach the state of annihilation in God, which is none other than being a total sacrifice in His Lordship. This entails renouncing one's own wishes, one's own good pleasure, and desire and servitude to the servants of the Abha Beauty, may my life be a ransom unto His loved ones!
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá explaining annihilation in God as renouncing one’s own wishes and serving the servants of the Abhá Beauty; opens the section on service.

All stations are metaphorical while this is reality; all ranks are conceptual while this is realization.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking that no station beyond servitude be attributed to him, all other stations being metaphorical; carries his handling of praise.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing servitude as the ornament of seen and unseen kingdoms and a garment clothing creation.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh testifying that, though created to attain God’s presence, He would be content if commanded to stand still; contentment with God’s command.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer of a heart melted from shame, confessing deeds that caused the dwellers of the cities of justice to lament.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praying that he and his namesake fulfil servitude outwardly and inwardly, in word and deed; the fuller of two overlapping selections.

selected.text: A prayer is being sent enclosed - please consider it. Mr. MacNutt has repented from that letter he wrote about Dr. Nutt, but it is a superficial repentance. selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calling a superficial repentance insufficient and recommending a Pauline repentance that leads to firmness; distinguishes true from outward repentance.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá explaining that willing submission and contentment are more specific than faith, and that the eye and truth of certainty shine only after submission; a substantive explanation of the station.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá directing that the opening of speech in gatherings be about his servitude, being free of every title but ‘Abdu’l-Bahá.

selected.text: Discover thou the mystery of God, and the secret of the All-Merciful, in the mirror of truth and the sea of servitude, and behold thou the world-enkindling ray of eminence and salvation in the dawning-place of thraldom and humility at the threshold of Almighty God. In the contingent world, even unto the very acme of the Placeless, loftiness, advancement and exaltation are impossible save on the wings of servitude; while nearness to the Holy Presence is unattainable unless the pinions of thraldom be unfurled.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá teaching that exaltation is impossible save on the wings of servitude and nearness unattainable without the pinions of thraldom.

selected.text: It is related that Fudayl of Khurasan was among the most wicked of men and a highwayman. He fell in love with a maiden and one night went to her, climbing over a wall. Then he heard someone reciting this verse: "Has not the time come for the hearts of those who believe to submit to the remembrance of God?" It affected his heart and he said: "Yes, my Lord, the time has indeed come!" He turned back, repented, and made his way to the Sacred House where he dwelt for thirty years until his spirit ascended to the supreme horizon
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s story of Fudayl, a highwayman turned back by a recited verse, who repented and dwelt thirty years at the Sacred House; the guide’s narrative example of conversion.

selected.text: O Lord! Make me evanescent, devout, prostrate, humble, serving, submissive, reverential, with face pressed to the dust, steadfast in true, essential, innate, inward, outward, primary, ultimate, eternal, everlasting servitude, for this is my highest summit and the utmost ascent to the apex of my greatest virtue. This is my eternal life, my everlasting existence, my joy, my gladness, the solace of mine eyes, the healing of my breast, the cure of my illness, the cooling of my burning, the rest of my spirit and my greatest victory.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s prayer to be made evanescent and steadfast in servitude, calling it his eternal life and greatest victory.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá addressing the humble ‘Ali and swearing that servitude to God is lordship over both worlds and bondage to Him freedom from all existence; the fuller of two overlapping selections.

My devotion is to arise to serve Thy Cause and to praise and glorify Thee amongst Thy servants - this too is my service. My effect is to spread Thy laws and to make mention of Thy chosen ones and to love Thy friends - this too is my effect
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s dialogue asking “What is thy service?” and answering with a life spent in God’s path, praise and love of His friends; a memorable account of service.

By Him Who holds my soul in His hand, this station is greater than all stations and is regarded as the most exalted of ranks in the sight of God, for through pure servitude the truth has been and will be established among humanity
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh calling all to move by the thread of servitude, the station greater than all stations through which truth is established among humanity.

selected.text: This is the day when the light of servitude shineth forth from the horizon's dawning-place, the time of the rising and radiance of the orb of unity and the blazing meteor in the unlimited firmament. Therefore, announce to all that in this radiant age each must be humble, meek, serving and worshipful before all, for worship of the Truth and servitude to the Ancient Beauty is conditional upon service to His servants.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá teaching that each must be humble and serving before all, since servitude to God depends on service to His servants; a foundational link between worship and service.

selected.text: A man asked another: "In what station are you?" He answered: "In the utmost happiness." "Where does this happiness come from?" selected.text: Cook Ting laid down his knife and replied, "What I care about is the Way, which goes beyond skill. When I first began cutting up oxen, all I could see was the ox itself. After three years I no longer saw the whole ox. And now--now I go at it by spirit and don't look with my eyes. Perception and understanding have come to a stop and spirit moves where it wants. I go along with the natural makeup, strike in the big hollows, guide the knife through the big openings, and follow things are they are. So I never touch the smallest ligament or tendon, much less a main joint."

importedAuthorityReview.finding: Compared BB00065 version 06b7250e908fb87c02857536374257fc4cbfc905bd0e52dd49730ad2b63b51eb, the Báb’s Letter on the apostasy of Mulla Jawad Vilyani (Suluk II), paragraphs 20 and 21, metadata Authorized N; both paragraphs are provisional, and the catalogue Translations list Gate of the Heart renderings including GOH.302-308x. The supplied wording, from Be thou contented, in utter acquiescence … to … this crystal, living water, carries the same teaching as paragraph20 (contentment with the Lord’s decree inwardly and outwardly, as content with misery as with glory, with poverty as with wealth, with exertion as with tranquility, and with sorrow as with joy) and the first sentence of paragraph21 (all moral science flows from this living water), in different wording: for example the catalogue’s “as content with abasement as with glory … with hardship as with ease” against the supplied “pleased with misery even as thou wouldst be with glory … with exertion as with tranquility.” No authority is asserted for either rendering. The catalogue rendering of paragraph20 in #740 is not retained, so this supplied version stands as the guide’s single reading of the passage. Keep on merit and preserve approximate status.

importedAuthorityReview.finding: No candidate catalogue record. It is an outside comparative text, not a Bahá’í writing, and no authority is asserted. Its wording is kept unchanged, and the guide’s reference to James Legge’s translation supplies the full story, including the cook’s caution at difficult joints. Keep on merit as the comparative closing reading.
